titulo_original: Epithelial tissues - Lining and covering quiz

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structures indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. This light micrograph shows a ciliated epithelium. Cilia can be distinguished from microvilli based on their height; 5-10 microns for cilia, ~1 micron for microvilli. In addition, each cilium has a dark-staining basal body that serves as the source of the microtubules that form the core of the cilium. Collectively, the basal bodies form a dark band just beneath the apical plasma membrane.

questoes.enunciado: Classify the epithelium indicated by the double arrow.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. In a pseudostratified epithelium all cells rest on the basement membrane, however they are of differing heights with some that reach the free surface and others that do not. It appears stratified, hence the classification “pseudostratified”, because nuclei appear at different heights. This epithelium displays the surface specialization, stereocilia.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the specific structure indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The lamina densa is a component of the basal lamina. It appears dark and "fuzzy" due to the Type IV collagen it contains. The lamina lucida lies just above the lamina densa and the reticular lamina just below.

questoes.enunciado: Classify the epithelium indicated by the arrow.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. This epithelium consists of a single row of cells which are extremely flattened. Therefore, this is an example of a simple squamous epithelium.

questoes.enunciado: Classify the epithelium indicated by the double arrow.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. This epithelium consists of many layers of cells, and the uppermost cells are squamous-shaped. No nuclei are visible in these uppermost cells, indicating that they are not living. Therefore, this is a stratified squamous, dry (or keratinized) epithelium.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structures indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Microvilli are extensions of the plasma membrane, that are approximately 1.0 micron in height. They contain a core of actin microfilaments and serve to increase surface area. When microvilli occur across the entire free surface of a cell (as seen here), they form a brush, or striated, border.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the rectangle.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The zonula occludens is the portion of the junctional complex which is closest to the free surface of the epithelium. The zonula occludens is a tight junction in which adjacent plasma membranes are held in close apposition by membrane proteins. This apposition forms a physical barrier that restricts the movement of soluble molecules into the intercellular space between cells.

questoes.enunciado: Classify the epithelium indicated by the double arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. This epithelium consists of a single role of tall columnar cells. In this image, this epithelium is lining the small intestine and the free surface is modified to form a brush border composed of closely packed microvilli. The increased surface area provided by the microvilli improves absorption of nutrients. Also present in this epithelium are unicellular, mucus-secreting goblet cells.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structures indicated by the ovals.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. An epithelial cell is anchored to its underlying basal lamina by hemidesmosomes. As the name indicates, these structures consist of one half of a desmosome. These adherent junctions are prominent in electron micrographs due to the large number of intermediate filaments and attachment proteins on the cytoplasmic surface of the membrane.

questoes.enunciado: Classify the epithelium indicated by the double arrow.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. This is a stratified epithelium as judged by the multiple layers of cells which become progressively more flattened (squamous) as they reach the free surface. This epithelium is classified as moist because the cells at the surface are living and retain their nuclei and cytoplasm.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structures indicated by arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Cilia appear as densely packed, hair-like, motile extensions from the apical cell surface, 5-10 microns in length. Each cilium has a basal body from which microtubules emanate, forming the core of the cilium, called the axoneme.

questoes.enunciado: Classify the epithelium indicated by the double arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. These cells all contact the basement membrane, and all are columnar in shape. Therefore, this is a simple columnar epithelium. This epithelium is distinguished from a stratified or pseudostratified epithelium, because the nuclei are all at the same height relative to the basal surface of the epithelium.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structures indicated by the rectangles.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Desmosomes are a type of adherent junction that serve to attach cell to one another. Desmosomes are a symmetrical junctions with mirror-image protein complexes in adjacent cells. Membrane proteins extend from these complexes to overlap with similar proteins from neighboring cells to provide the attachment.

questoes.enunciado: Classify the epithelium indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. These tubules consist of a single row of cells which are of nearly equal height and width. Therefore, this is a simple cuboidal epithelium. While the cell membranes are not discernable, the overall shape of the cell can be inferred from the shape of the nucleus. In this case, the spherical nucleus indicates that the cell is box-shaped rather than flat or column-shaped.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structures indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Cilia appear as densely packed, hair-like, motile extensions from the apical cell surface, 5-10 microns in length. Each cilium has a basal body from which microtubules emanate forming the core of the cilium, called the axoneme. Seen in this light microscopic image, the basal bodies collectively appear as a dark band along the apical surface of the cell.

questoes.enunciado: Classify the epithelium indicated by the double arrow.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. This is a stratified epithelium as judged by the multiple layers of cells which become progressively more flattened (squamous) as they reach the free surface. This epithelium is classified as moist because the cells at the surface are living and retain their nuclei and cytoplasm. A nucleated squamous cell being sloughed from the surface is visible in this image.

questoes.enunciado: Classify the epithelium indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. This epithelium consists of a single row of cells which are extremely flattened. Therefore, this is an example of a simple squamous epithelium. Endothelium is a specific name that denotes the unique simple squamous epithelium that lines blood vessels. The epithelium indicated here lines a specific segment of the kidney tubules (nephrons).

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: CORRECT.  This light micrograph shows a ciliated epithelium.  Cilia can be distinguished from microvilli based on their height; 5-10 microns for cilia, ~1 micron for microvilli.  In addition, each cilium has a dark-staining basal body that serves as the source of the microtubules that form the core of the cilium.  Collectively, the basal bodies form a dark band just beneath the apical plasma membrane.
